# V01 golden corpus — what the parser does today.
#
# Format:  verdict  pattern_id  arg_hash  sql
#   verdict     "ok", or the StatusCode name the parse was rejected with.
#   pattern_id  16 hex digits, or "-" when FingerprintOf() returns nothing
#   arg_hash    (leading word not SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE, or the text does
#               not lex). Both columns are "-" together or neither is.
#   sql         rest of the line, verbatim. `\n` is an escape for a real
#               newline; nothing else is escaped.
#
# Which columns may move, and when:
#
#   verdict     may move, *deliberately*, when a task makes a reserved form
#               supported or gives it its own code. The lines marked
#               "[V05]", "[V07]" and so on are the ones expected to flip,
#               and each names the task that owns the flip. A verdict that
#               moves without its task is a regression.
#
#   pattern_id  must not move from one hash to another, ever: the v2
#   arg_hash    language is additive shape, and a moved hash retires every
#               stored waystone. Two permitted transitions. "-" to a hash,
#               when a statement that could not be lexed becomes lexable
#               (V04's dot token) — nothing already stored changes meaning,
#               since a shape that hashed to X still hashes to X. And a
#               hash that could never be stored may move (TY3 phase 2's
#               numeric token): a statement that lexed but parsed in no
#               production was fingerprintable yet unrecordable, so its
#               hash names nothing on disk. The second is the one to argue
#               carefully — fingerprint.cpp's kNumLit note is the shape of
#               the argument required.
#
# Verdicts here were derived by reading src/parser/parser.cpp; hashes were
# recorded from the build. See tests/parser_golden_test.cpp for why those
# two are treated differently.

# ---- CREATE TABLE — accepted -----------------------------------------------
# CREATE is not a patternable leading word, so every line here is "-".
ok	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int)
ok	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int, name varchar)
ok	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id bigint, a int, b varchar, c uint64)
ok	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) HEAP
ok	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) BTREE
ok	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) heap
ok	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int);
ok	-	-	create table t (id int)
# The key-mode words after the mode's removal (heap-and-tuple.md §4.1,
# 2026-08-25). `EXPLICIT` still parses and now does nothing - it states
# what every relation is. `ASSIGNED` names a mode that no longer exists and
# is refused here, `Unsupported` with its byte: ignoring it would be
# accepting a spelling and enforcing something else. No hash moved either
# way, so kFingerprintVersion did not (fingerprint_test.cpp).
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) ASSIGNED
ok	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) EXPLICIT
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) HEAP ASSIGNED
ok	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) BTREE EXPLICIT
ok	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) EXPLICIT BTREE
ok	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) explicit btree

# ---- CREATE TABLE — rejected -----------------------------------------------
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE t (id int)
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE (id int)
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE 42 (id int)
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t id int
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t ()
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (42 int)
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id)
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int,)
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) FOO
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE
# [PK03] one word per category, and an unknown word after both still
# reaches the trailing-garbage check.
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) HEAP BTREE
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) BTREE BTREE
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) ASSIGNED EXPLICIT
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) EXPLICIT EXPLICIT
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) BTREE EXPLICIT FOO
# [V11] gains WITH (k = v); today the option list is trailing garbage.
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE TABLE t (id int) WITH (PHYSICAL_OPTIMIZER = ON)

# [BLK] Multi-row VALUES (docs/spec/bulkinsert.md BI5): row count is not
# part of the template, so the N-row statement carries the 1-row
# statement's pattern_id - the same hash as the lines above - and later
# rows' values fold into arg_hash only. Every pre-existing hash this
# suppression moved belonged to a statement that parsed in no production
# (fingerprintable, never storable), the bump rule's permitted second
# transition; the moved lines below say so where they sit.
ok	a2266ff85c0a8df6	78f79099c419719c	INSERT INTO t VALUES (1), (2)
ok	c323a07930901e82	3042954c6216ee3a	INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'a'), (2, 'b'), (3, 'c')

# [BLK] The two hashes BI5's suppression moved, both never storable
# (neither ever parsed): `... (1) extra` now hashes as the plain 1-row
# insert, since `extra` sits past the first group and folds nothing; the
# column-list form's first group is `(a, b)`, so its VALUES row became

# [V15 — done] a column on the right of a comparison. Spec I10 describes
# the filter surface as `col op {slot}`, but §2's *correlated* subquery is
# written `WHERE inner.col = outer.col` and cannot be spelled without
# this - a feature J1 put in scope cannot be unreachable from the grammar,
# so the two are reconciled in favour of §2. Executing one still needs the
# step chain; the dispatcher refuses it until V17 rather than comparing
# against an unset value.
ok	6c0be26239157118	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE a = b
InvalidArgument	46749465e53887c0	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t extra
InvalidArgument	92e35026b1321260	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t; SELECT * FROM u
# [V04 — done] the dot token. These three lines are the whole permitted
# "-" -> hash transition: before V04 a '.' lexed as kError, so no statement
# containing one had a fingerprint at all. Nothing already stored changed
# meaning and kFingerprintVersion stayed at 1. Every other line on this
# page kept its hash across V04, including the ones carrying the seven
# newly reserved words - which is the evidence that reserving a word is a
# grammar change and not a fingerprint change.
InvalidArgument	b825796128f262f6	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE a . b
# [V06 — done] a qualified column in a select list.
ok	62bd6d094d21d3db	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT t.id FROM t
# A comma FROM list is a cross join, which this grammar does not have.
# Not reached by V05 and not planned: joins are written JOIN ... ON.
InvalidArgument	2e2a3c1453705f3b	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t, u
# [V05 — done] joins and aliases parse. These two flipped
# InvalidArgument -> ok, and no hash moved with them: reserving LEFT,
# RIGHT, FULL and OUTER alongside changed no pattern_id, which is the
# second demonstration of V04's keyword design.
#
# [V06 — done] and the JOIN line flipped the second time, as predicted:
# ok -> Unsupported. `SELECT *` is ambiguous across relations, so an
# explicit list became mandatory as soon as there was one to write. Two
# deliberate flips, two tasks; no hash moved in either.
Unsupported	e9242b44747c5e35	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t JOIN u ON t.id = u.id
ok	a91c9b42e1642b7c	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t AS a
# [V07] predicate-position subqueries.
ok	e0208a3774f7afe5	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM u)
ok	5b6a4489f043e0d7	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM u)
ok	d9e6d16ebc7df09d	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM u)
# [V08 — BETWEEN half done] The IN-list half is still open and still fails.
#
# **The hashes did not move when BETWEEN became parseable**, and that is the
# whole reason this line stayed pinned while its verdict flipped: BETWEEN has
# lexed as a reserved keyword since V04, and a keyword hashes exactly as the
# identifier it used to be. Becoming *parseable* changes no shape stream.
InvalidArgument	b87254b3cae4a5b8	78f79099c419719c	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id IN (1, 2)
ok	af3f6ac336bb68d8	78f78f99c4196fe9	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id BETWEEN 1 AND 5
ok	e55ef6c0ffc6290e	78f78f99c4196fe9	SELECT * FROM t WHERE v BETWEEN 1 AND 5
ok	ba36feab6d6a3125	2435274fd957b578	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id BETWEEN 1 AND 5 AND name = 'x'
ok	4aa155c62d488ef9	78f78f99c4196fe9	SELECT * FROM t AS a WHERE a.id BETWEEN 1 AND 5
# BETWEEN with a missing AND, or a missing bound, is a syntax error naming
# the position - not a silent one-sided range. Both still *lex*, so both
# still have a fingerprint: refusing to parse is not refusing to hash.
InvalidArgument	5be869c8076bff1f	b5d414774c8002cc	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id BETWEEN 1
InvalidArgument	97eadbe49c827e47	78f78f99c4196fe9	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id BETWEEN 1 5
InvalidArgument	4338879b6a60f25b	78f79099c419719c	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = 1 OR id = 2
# [V09] pagination. The tail parses since 2026-08-10, and the two hashes
# that predate it did not move: `order`, `by`, `asc`, `limit` and `offset`
# were always ordinary identifiers, so becoming parseable changed no shape
# stream - the verdicts flipped with their task, the V08 precedent. The
# counts are slots (I11): LIMIT 10 and LIMIT 20 share a pattern_id below.
# DESC, an aggregated statement's tail and a subquery's stay refused.
#
# [OB1] the general ORDER BY. DESC and a multi-key list flipped to `ok` -
# their two hashes below did not move either, for exactly the reason the
# V09 flips did not: `desc` was always an ordinary identifier and a comma
# was always a comma, so what changed is the verdict and not the shape.
# An ordinal stays refused, and for a reason DESC never had: it names a
# select-list position, which is a second spelling of a thing that already
# has one. An aggregated statement's tail also stays refused, which is what
# keeps aggregate.md section 10's decision open.
ok	2014153a5d44a3d2	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY id
ok	cfd92d5cf2657bf9	183c9abf547928f7	SELECT * FROM t LIMIT 10
ok	cfd92d5cf2657bf9	183288bf5470b5dc	SELECT * FROM t LIMIT 20
ok	a2ab37bd0b9912d1	6a2936eff68a8d8a	SELECT * FROM t LIMIT 10 OFFSET 5
ok	d1d97970aff68c0c	b5d410774c7ffc00	SELECT * FROM t OFFSET 5
ok	9e51e28ff0f77902	90e9577200715765	SELECT a FROM t WHERE a = 1 ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT 2 OFFSET 1
ok	7f56cd80953c49c8	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT limit, offset FROM t
ok	44d61d637a45b7d0	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY id DESC
Unsupported	e967d58b511229ec	b5d414774c8002cc	SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY 1

Unsupported	53268d89f9272838	b5d410774c7ffc00	SELECT b, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY b LIMIT 5
Unsupported	da3c546ef95221a8	b5d416774c800632	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM u LIMIT 3)
InvalidArgument	cfd92d5cf2657bf9	184a11bf54847d88	SELECT * FROM t LIMIT -1

# [AG01] Aggregates. I14 is resolved by docs/spec/aggregate.md, so this
# parses now — and the hash did not move, which is the whole of §2's
# fingerprint argument: nothing was reserved and no token type was added,
# so `count` lexes as the identifier it always was.
ok	1dbdfb79bafd459e	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t
ok	e98a95e073db2017	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT b, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY b
ok	489356a113ef4e44	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT SUM(DISTINCT x) FROM t
# A column may still be named `count` or `group`: a function head is a name
# from the set *followed by a paren*, and no production puts a paren after a
# column reference.
ok	ff41a860584dc5e0	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT count FROM t
ok	060af4ce805c88ca	b5d414774c8002cc	SELECT * FROM t WHERE group = 1
# AVG folds since 2026-08-07 (aggregate.md §3.4): the verdict flipped
# with its task, and the hash did not move - AVG was always an ordinary
# identifier to the lexer, which is what the non-reservation rule buys.
# The type rule (decimal columns only) is the compiler's, invisible here.
ok	91fa1130f96f7220	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT AVG(x) FROM t
ok	c827c5fe23c991df	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT AVG(DISTINCT x) FROM t
# HAVING and ORDER BY over aggregated output. Both were refusals - AG7, and
# §2's [PROPOSED] ORDER BY row - and both parse since 2026-08-24
# (docs/inflight/in-progress/workplan-having.md HV-1): the verdicts flipped with the task that
# intended them, and **neither hash moved**, because HAVING lexes as the
# ordinary identifier it always was and a HAVING literal is a slot exactly
# as a WHERE literal is. Same evidence AVG's flip above carries, and the
# reason `kFingerprintVersion` did not move for either.
ok	fe758a469156cb26	b5d414774c8002cc	SELECT b, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY b HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ok	61193a3cf78e857f	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT b, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY b ORDER BY b

# ---- ALTER (docs/spec/alter.md AL1, AL7) -----------------------------------
# ALTER is not a patternable leading word, so every line is "-". The
# refusal class is the feature: v1 is catalog-only, and ADD/DROP answer a
# positioned Unsupported carrying invariant 13's reason.

ok	-	-	ALTER TABLE t RENAME COLUMN a TO b

Unsupported	-	-	ALTER TABLE t DROP COLUMN a

InvalidArgument	-	-	ALTER t RENAME TO u

# ---- Joins and aliases (V05) ------------------------------------------------
# New forms, recorded here the moment they became reachable. Placeholder
# hashes were never written for these: they were added after V04 and their
# values came off the build, like every other row on this page.
#
# Accepted. Written with explicit select lists since [V06 — done]: these
# said `SELECT *` when V05 added them, and all five flipped to Unsupported
# when the star rule landed. Rewritten rather than left flipped, so this
# section keeps testing what it is named for - that a join parses. The
# star-over-a-join refusal has its own lines in the V06 section below.
ok	e4edb2c8b4eb5d3c	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT t.id FROM t JOIN u ON t.id = u.id JOIN v ON u.id = v.id
ok	5b47556ce9244d2e	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT a.id FROM t AS a JOIN u AS b ON a.id = b.id
# The self-join. It is expressible only because the duplicate-binding rule
# below refuses the version without aliases.
ok	a9c615e6411952e5	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT a.id, b.id FROM t AS a JOIN t AS b ON a.id = b.id
ok	ee7a5fe23cf0e3b8	cbf29ce484222325	select t.id from t join u on t.id = u.id
ok	09203711bb6e1327	b5d414774c8002cc	SELECT t.id FROM t JOIN u ON t.id = u.id WHERE t.id = 1
#
# Unsupported — a well-formed statement this engine declines, each with the
# byte position of what it declined. Distinct from InvalidArgument, which
# means "look for a typo".
Unsupported	3597f4484605402f	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t LEFT JOIN u ON t.id = u.id
Unsupported	8aec5874566e99c1	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t RIGHT JOIN u ON t.id = u.id
Unsupported	f6e1013d24de0aa0	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t FULL OUTER JOIN u ON t.id = u.id
# One relation named twice with no way to tell the occurrences apart.
Unsupported	a297f62980ae08d9	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t JOIN t ON t.id = t.id
Unsupported	ec10eded05cdb080	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t AS a JOIN u AS a ON a.id = a.id
# An unqualified ON column names no relation; V14 owns resolution.
Unsupported	f0039522b21c1cd9	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t JOIN u ON id = u.id
#
# Rejected outright — malformed, not merely undoable.
InvalidArgument	a1bf63b73d194ba6	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t JOIN u
InvalidArgument	bbaee1ae8ff21642	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t JOIN u ON t.id

InvalidArgument	7c7f9c7acd451965	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t AS
InvalidArgument	d1f04baacc6a2a05	182b9abf546ab5c4	SELECT * FROM t AS 42
# INNER is not a reserved word and no production consumes it, so this is
# trailing garbage rather than an accepted synonym. Spec I9 names only the
# outer keywords as reserved.

# ---- Projection and qualified names (V06) -----------------------------------
# Accepted: an explicit select list, qualified or bare, and a WHERE column

ok	e1d213b42ea6b631	78f79099c419719c	UPDATE t SET a = 1 WHERE t.id = 2
#
# Unsupported — `SELECT *` has no answer once there is more than one
# relation for it to span, and written order being the client's to choose
# is exactly what makes it unanswerable.
Unsupported	7bfb6efe6f64c69c	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t AS a JOIN u AS b ON a.id = b.id
#
# Rejected — malformed select lists. `SELECT *, a` and `SELECT a, *` are
# here because star is a whole select list, never a list element.
InvalidArgument	d591805ceb2c9c23	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT FROM t
InvalidArgument	65a9a93fb6b45224	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT a, FROM t
InvalidArgument	a41e0c3299fb216c	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT a b FROM t
InvalidArgument	4518328abb44759c	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT a., b FROM t
InvalidArgument	ca77cd098eb35051	182b9abf546ab5c4	SELECT 42 FROM t
InvalidArgument	d4d7ff16193af251	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT a, * FROM t
InvalidArgument	5efeb056abe3ea93	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT *, a FROM t
# A SET target names a column of the one relation UPDATE reads, so a
# qualifier on it says nothing the statement does not already say.
InvalidArgument	86430a5c1793ac6c	b5d414774c8002cc	UPDATE t SET t.a = 1

# ---- Predicate-position subqueries (V07) ------------------------------------
# The four accepted forms, plus correlation and nesting.
ok	17da6791a10fc738	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id != (SELECT id FROM u)
ok	01f584b45df39b0d	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT t_id FROM u)
ok	d93248f61bcdef44	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM u)
ok	cf8afe3c02d3ddbc	b5d414774c8002cc	SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM u WHERE u.t_id = 1)
ok	9bb9650d93cef8b5	2a44fca2241ecfc1	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = 1 AND EXISTS (SELECT * FROM u) AND name = 'x'
ok	c4aef8669030844b	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM u) AND EXISTS (SELECT * FROM v)
ok	efbc8ed4f64badef	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id IN (SELECT a.id FROM u AS a JOIN v AS b ON a.id = b.id)
ok	5094fc7111efa6ee	b5d414774c8002cc	UPDATE t SET a = 1 WHERE id IN (SELECT t_id FROM u)
ok	e0208a3774f7afe5	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM u);
# At the depth cap (4 nested blocks) and one past it.
ok	372af9a2b308c984	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t))))
Unsupported	a6d47bc00b1c1048	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM t)))))
#
# Nesting outside predicate position. Each is Unsupported with a position,
# never a bare syntax error: the relation-reference production must not
# reach the statement production, and WITH must not lex as a statement
# head. A derived table's result would have to become a relation with a
# schema, probed by something other than a pk - which is the execution
# model, not an unimplemented feature.
Unsupported	8395ef7c84c6184e	b5d414774c8002cc	SELECT * FROM t WHERE NOT id = 1
Unsupported	6a572ac142c50425	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t JOIN (SELECT * FROM u) ON t.id = u.id
Unsupported	ea325ba2b616a269	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM u)
Unsupported	-	-	WITH x AS (SELECT * FROM u) SELECT * FROM x
#
# Malformed. `IN (1, 2)` is [V08]'s value list and stays rejected here.
InvalidArgument	d7a6bdcced6fcc02	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM u
InvalidArgument	b1ee15b5a9bc7449	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS ()
InvalidArgument	9660f26161090c96	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS
InvalidArgument	ae06d22736a3755c	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id IN ()
InvalidArgument	e0208a3774f7afe5	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT * FROM u;)
InvalidArgument	d91afc534d177df6	cbf29ce484222325	INSERT INTO t VALUES ((SELECT id FROM u))
InvalidArgument	9964d7fce0f74496	cbf29ce484222325	UPDATE t SET a = (SELECT id FROM u)
#
# [AG01] Aggregates in a subquery. V07's done-condition asked for
# Unsupported with a position on these and they used to give a bare syntax
# error, because I14 had not decided whether aggregates were excluded from
# the grammar or reserved-and-rejected. AG8 decides it: the forms parse and
# are refused *as aggregation*, permanently for v1 — a fold inside a
# sub-chain puts an aggregation boundary where the execution model has none.
Unsupported	009742650befee6a	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM u)
Unsupported	dd4d901ce6b336cc	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM u GROUP BY id)

# ---- Top level — rejected --------------------------------------------------
InvalidArgument	-	-	\n
InvalidArgument	-	-	-- comment only
InvalidArgument	-	-	42
InvalidArgument	-	-	*
InvalidArgument	-	-	?
InvalidArgument	-	-	(SELECT * FROM t)
# [CREATE PATTERN] `DROP` became a statement head; [DT01] made TABLE one
# of its objects (docs/spec/drop-table.md), so the verdict flipped with
# its task - `DROP` is not a patternable head and the hashes stay "-".
ok	-	-	DROP TABLE t
ok	-	-	drop table t;
InvalidArgument	-	-	SELECTX * FROM t
# [txn T10] DELETE became a statement head - the transaction work needed it
# (docs/spec/txn.md section 10 tests it), so the flip is owned by that task
# rather than by a parser one. It stays unfingerprinted: adding a
# patternable leading word does **not** move any hash already stored, which
# is the case fingerprint.hpp's bump rule names explicitly.
ok	-	-	DELETE FROM t WHERE id = 1
# [V12] session and admin statements.
InvalidArgument	-	-	SET DURABILITY STRICT
InvalidArgument	-	-	SHOW TABLES

# ---- CREATE PATTERN / DROP PATTERN ----------------------------------------
#
# A declaration is not patternable itself - its leading word is CREATE - so
# both hash columns are "-" throughout. What *is* fingerprinted is the body,
# separately, and fingerprint_test.cpp owns that property; these lines pin
# the grammar.
ok	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p($f int64) OF SELECT id FROM t WHERE id = $f
ok	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p() OF SELECT * FROM t
ok	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p($a int64, $b varchar) OF SELECT id, name FROM t WHERE id = $a AND name = $b
ok	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p($f int64) WITH (pinned = on) OF SELECT id FROM t WHERE id = $f
ok	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p($f int64) WITH (pinned = off, expected_instances = 100000) OF SELECT id FROM t WHERE id = $f
ok	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p($f int64) OF SELECT a.id FROM t AS a JOIN u AS b ON a.id = b.id WHERE a.id = $f
ok	-	-	DROP PATTERN p
# A parameter used twice is legal - a readability device, not a constraint:
# the fingerprint cannot enforce that two slots carry the same value (spec
# section 3.3), and the doc says so rather than letting anyone mistake it
# for a bug.
ok	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p($f int64) OF SELECT id FROM t WHERE id = $f AND other = $f

# The type annotation is mandatory - inference from first use was
# considered and rejected (spec section 2).
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p($f) OF SELECT * FROM t
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p(f int64) OF SELECT * FROM t
# WITH must precede OF: the body runs to end of statement, which is what
# means the parser never has to find where a SELECT ends.
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p($f int64) OF SELECT * FROM t WITH (pinned = on)
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p($f int64) SELECT * FROM t
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE PATTERN ($f int64) OF SELECT * FROM t
InvalidArgument	-	-	DROP PATTERN
# v1 declares SELECT-class bodies only; INSERT/UPDATE patterns are deferred
# (spec section 9), gated by validation rather than by the fingerprint.
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE PATTERN p($f int64) OF INSERT INTO t VALUES (1)

# ---- $param outside a declaration -----------------------------------------
#
# The token exists and fingerprints - it is reserved for the extended
# protocol's named binds (D4) - but no production outside a CREATE PATTERN
# body accepts it. Note the hashes are present, not "-": these statements
# lex fine, they just do not parse, which is the same state a bare `?` in
# value position was already in.
#
# The first line's pattern_id is 0212b03badb413ad, which is *the same hash*
# the `= 1` and `= ?` lines above carry. That is spec section 3.2's whole
# claim, sitting in the corpus where it cannot rot: a declared body and the
# live traffic it is meant to match reduce to one pattern.
Unsupported	0212b03badb413ad	cbf29ce484222325	SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = $x
Unsupported	ae34f9ce9d472ac9	b5d414774c8002cc	UPDATE t SET c = $x WHERE id = 1

# ---- Bare numeric literals (TY3 phase 2) -----------------------------------
#
# `12.34` is one token and one value: the quoted string of its spelling.
# The first two lines pin the whole design in corpus form - the bare and
# quoted spellings carry the *same* pattern_id and the *same* arg_hash,
# because they are one statement, not a collision.
#
# Before this token, digit-dot-digit lexed as int, dot, int: fingerprintable
# but parsed by no production. Fusing it moved those statements' hashes -
# the corpus rule's second permitted transition, "a hash that could never be
# stored may move", argued in fingerprint.cpp and pinned by
# fingerprint_test.cpp's TheNumericTokenNeededNoFingerprintVersionBump.
ok	ecba24c306c70be5	a3c68932ec2dc068	SELECT * FROM t WHERE amt = 12.34
ok	ecba24c306c70be5	a3c68932ec2dc068	SELECT * FROM t WHERE amt = '12.34'
ok	ecba24c306c70be5	100a442a17d84421	SELECT * FROM t WHERE amt = -0.5
ok	d6bd36cbdaeee580	66f3ec47f0d82909	SELECT * FROM t WHERE amt BETWEEN 1.00 AND 2.50
ok	c323a07930901e82	f7f9adb5d61121fd	INSERT INTO t VALUES (12.34, 'x')
ok	ae34f9ce9d472ac9	46ac44ad760bc8f1	UPDATE t SET c = 12.34 WHERE id = 1
# Digits are required on both sides of the point, so these stay the parse
# errors they always were - and their hashes are the pre-fusion token
# sequences, unchanged.
InvalidArgument	0758626484394051	183c9cbf54792c5d	SELECT * FROM t WHERE amt = 12.
InvalidArgument	0765f6648444c629	b5d410774c7ffc00	SELECT * FROM t WHERE amt = .5
InvalidArgument	b46f83ccad484d09	ae5e91f4b62d26a6	SELECT * FROM t WHERE amt = 1.2.3

# ---- CREATE INDEX / DROP INDEX (docs/spec/index.md §10) --------------------
#
# Every line here is new, and not one pre-existing line moved: `index`,
# `covering` and `unique` reach the lexer as ordinary identifiers, exactly as
# the aggregate function names did, so no token sequence changed meaning and
# kFingerprintVersion did not move. A column may still be named any of them,
# which the line below the refusals pins.
ok	-	-	CREATE INDEX by_owner ON accounts (owner)
ok	-	-	CREATE INDEX ix ON t (b, a, c)
ok	-	-	CREATE INDEX ix ON t (a) COVERING (b, c)
ok	-	-	CREATE INDEX ix ON t (a) covering (b)
ok	-	-	CREATE INDEX ix ON t (a);
ok	-	-	DROP INDEX by_owner
ok	-	-	CREATE INDEX unique ON t (index) COVERING (covering)
ok	98c09327562a9560	b5d414774c8002cc	SELECT index FROM t WHERE covering = 1
# UNIQUE is refused at its own byte: enforcing uniqueness makes the index a
# constraint, which would let an index failure abort a write (IX11).
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ix ON t (a)
# A cap refuses and never truncates (spec §11), with the offending column's
# position - which is the one thing only this layer knows.
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE INDEX ix ON t (a, b, c, d, e)
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE INDEX ix ON t (a) COVERING (b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j)
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE INDEX ix (a)
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE INDEX ix ON t
InvalidArgument	-	-	DROP INDEX

# ---- CREATE ASSERTION / DROP ASSERTION (docs/spec/assertion.md §3) ---------
#
# Every line here is "-  -": assertion DDL carries no pattern, because its
# leading word is CREATE. The point of the block is the *verdicts*, and that
# every pre-existing line in this file passed unchanged - which is the whole
# evidence AST02 owes for "DML fingerprints are unaffected".
#
# `assertion`, `check` and `group` are matched by text and are not keywords,
# so they are still usable as names; the fourth line is that, and the DML
# lines below it are the half that actually carries a hash.
ok	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION lim ON purchases GROUP BY (user_id, product_id) CHECK COUNT(*) <= 5
ok	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION credit ON orders GROUP BY (user_id) CHECK SUM(amount) < 1000
ok	-	-	create assertion a on t group by (x) check count(*) <= 1;
ok	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION assertion ON check GROUP BY (assertion, check) CHECK COUNT(*) <= 1
ok	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (c0, c1, c2, c3, c4, c5, c6, c7, c8, c9, c10) CHECK COUNT(*) <= 1
ok	-	-	DROP ASSERTION lim

# Reserved and refused: a form this engine understands and declines, each at
# its own byte. AS11 (a lower bound would have to be checked on DELETE),
# AS3/AS7 (timing clauses), §10 (aggregates that are not incrementally
# maintainable, or are not bounds at all).
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(*) > 5
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK SUM(v) >= 5
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(*) <= 1 DEFERRABLE
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(*) <= 1 NOT DEFERRABLE
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(*) <= 1 NOT VALID
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK MIN(v) <= 1
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK AVG(v) <= 1
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(v) <= 1
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(DISTINCT v) <= 1

# Wrong rather than reserved: no ceiling in any direction, a bound that is not
# a non-negative integer literal, a predicate that could never admit a row
# (§3.1 - a group holds at least one row, so COUNT(*) = 0 is unsatisfiable),
# and a missing mandatory clause.
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(*) != 5
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(*) <= -1
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(*) <= 1.5
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(*) = 0
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(*) < 1
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK SUM(*) <= 1
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK TOTAL(v) <= 1
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t CHECK COUNT(*) <= 1
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x)
InvalidArgument	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY () CHECK COUNT(*) <= 1
InvalidArgument	-	-	DROP ASSERTION

# A SUM bound of zero is *not* degenerate: an int64 column may hold negative
# values, so no non-negative bound is provably unsatisfiable.
ok	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK SUM(v) <= 0

# [AS11 rev. 2026-08-08] `=` moved from ok to Unsupported. It parsed and was
# documented as meaning `aggregate <= N`; that reinterpreted what the operator
# wrote, and enforcing real equality needs the lower-bound half v1 excludes.
# A verdict moving with the task that owns it, which is what this column is for.
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK COUNT(*) = 5
Unsupported	-	-	CREATE ASSERTION a ON t GROUP BY (x) CHECK SUM(v) = 100

# ---- Physical optimizer surface (docs/spec/physical-optimizer.md, PX06) ----
# SHOW is a dispatcher verb, not SQL - the verdict matches SHOW TABLES above -
# and `relayout` stays an ordinary identifier: no keyword moved for the report
# surface, which the two SELECTs pin by fingerprinting like any column/table.
InvalidArgument	-	-	SHOW RELAYOUT
InvalidArgument	-	-	SHOW RELAYOUT trades
ok	4b08123e9d144ab4	b5d416774c800632	SELECT relayout FROM t WHERE relayout = 3
ok	512d110d0175126f	b5d412774c7fff66	SELECT * FROM relayout WHERE id = 7
